Output written to `/home/mara/cwe-bench/pipelines/stacking/out/screener-ds-rescreen/2085.json`.

- **Trust decision:** an OAuth2 token URL that receives `client_id`/`client_secret` must be https or literal-loopback http (`utcp_http/_security.py:96-112`), but at the pinned commit it is enforced only on discovery/invocation URLs — never on `OAuth2Auth.token_url`, at conversion or at any token POST.
- **pattern_fit:** `A` — one advisory about "OpenAPI conversion" whose fix lands at 7 sites across 5 separate `_handle_oauth2` implementations in 3 packages (utcp-http, utcp-gql, utcp-websocket), from an unvalidated converter producer to distant runtime sinks.
- **Strongest lever:** the report points at the converter, but the protection must be replicated at each protocol's token sink — gql/websocket look out of scope (utcp-gql has no `utcp.plugins` entry point, an empty `INCOMPLETE` marker, and is absent from CI), and a converter-only or `OAuth2Auth`-model fix breaks `${TOKEN_URL}` variable injection that is substituted only after config load.
- **Biggest red flag:** `tiny_repo` (~20.2k Python lines / ~1 MB of source, estimated from line counts since no shell was available); no reachable Pattern-B route exists — the MCP plugin's duplicate unguarded token sink is dead code, so it was logged as injection room only.
